Help & scope

Build settlements with the Spectacular Settlements rules: roll everything at once, or work card by card. Everything you generate is DM preparation; the Summary viewer makes a separate player version.

Quick start

Covers Trading Posts, Villages, Towns, Cities and Fortresses (Keeps, Castles and Strongholds), the fortress map and the DM toolkit. Not included yet: full Keep room layouts, Capitals, Stronghold upgrades, and sending changes back to the Codex.

  1. Add a settlement. In Settlement collection, choose a type (Trading Post, Village, Town, City or Fortress) and press Add blank settlement.
  2. Roll it. Press Roll all unrolled fields to fill every table, or use Roll unrolled in this section on one tab at a time.
  3. Make it yours. Reroll a card, choose a book outcome instead, or lock the results you like before rerolling the rest.
  4. Settle the open decisions. Anything shown in amber is waiting for your choice.
  5. Save and use it. Save collection JSON is your backup. Summary opens the printable views (index card, cut sheet, full write-up, handouts and atlas) in a DM or Player version.

Find and review

Find in collection searches saved names, aliases, book types and NPC connections. Filter by settlement or record kind; inactive places are hidden until included. Results show their settlement and district context. Open a result to edit its existing record.

Review current settlement links to active unresolved fields, decisions and the Castle review. Optional writing prompts are listed separately. These prompts are preparation suggestions, not additional generation rules.

Searching and reviewing roll nothing and do not change saves. Opening a result in another settlement uses the normal undoable settlement switch. In the builder section navigation, Left/Right moves between sections; Home/End opens the first/last section. Tab and Enter continue to work normally.

Rolling and choosing results

Each card is one book table

  • Roll rolls that table's die. You can also type a die result you rolled yourself into the raw-die box (under More).
  • Choose book outcome sets the result directly. A chosen outcome replaces the roll: the die is cleared, Roll is disabled, and incoming modifiers no longer apply. The card shows a quill and “Chosen by the GM.”
  • Set the dropdown back to Choose… to return the card to unrolled; no earlier roll is restored.
  • The line under each result explains it in plain words, for example “Rolled 14 on a d20, +2 for Age → 16.” The full technical formula is kept in Source table and roll history.

Modifiers, adjustments and notes

  • Earlier results can modify later tables. If a modifier's source hasn't been rolled yet, the card waits for it (“Waiting for …”).
  • The book makes modifiers optional: switch one off under Modifiers, notes, and custom wording and give a short reason.
  • A GM adjustment adds to or subtracts from the roll before the table is read.
  • Custom wording and notes are for your own descriptions; they never change the mechanics.

Locking results

  • Click the padlock on a card to lock its result. Reroll all unlocked fields and the section reroll buttons will leave it alone.
  • Only cards with a result can be locked. A locked result can still change if a card it depends on changes; choose a book outcome to fix it completely.
  • Pressing a card's own Roll button always rolls it.

Tidy cards and decisions

  • Tidy cards (next to Roll all) tucks dice inputs and drawers behind More on rolled cards. Turn it off to show everything.
  • Amber marks a decision only you can make, such as choosing a venue, a category for a bonus site, or which printed range applies.
  • Some printed tables overlap (for example Trading Post demographics and Village Age at 10). When a roll lands on an overlap, pick which range applies; your die is kept.

Points of interest

  • Every site appears as a card showing its business, how it got there (Default, Rolled, Bonus or GM) and its quality in stars. Click a card to open its editor below.
  • In a City, sites are grouped by district, each headed by the district itself, with outside-the-city sites in their own group.
  • Location counts and generation settings changes allocations, water access and optional quality.
  • When a count goes down, the extra sites become inactive rather than deleted. Tick Show inactive to see them. Saved JSON keeps inactive sites; DM Markdown leaves them out.
  • Add your own places with Add GM site; these sit outside the book's counts.
  • Optional quality applies to shops, services, worship and GM sites.
  • Renaming a site keeps its read-only Book type. Reset the name beside Name; Aliases, record Type and Scale are in the collapsed Record details drawer. Location pickers use names and book types, grouped by category or City district. Unfinished sites are marked “type not chosen”.

NPCs, names and connections

People and ties

  • Create draft NPC on Records creates an untied person. Choose the Location and press Add connection. Create NPC for this site makes a connection only to the selected point of interest.
  • Each NPC has one connection per location. Changing its type or role updates that connection; use Edit to move it, or Remove to delete it. Connections carry their type and title, including settlement-level ties such as ruler / Jarl. Redundant owner / proprietor titles are cleared on load.
  • Collection NPCs are always available. Tick Include Codex NPCs to include Codex identities, grouped and searchable by region; entries without a region appear under Unsorted. This viewer preference is remembered separately from saves.
  • Draft NPCs are shared across the collection: editing one updates every settlement that uses it. Permanent IDs survive renaming.
  • Imported identities bring names and IDs only, never party knowledge or biographies. Established Codex identities keep their names.
  • Hired-help teams and guilds are groups; they don't automatically become single NPCs.

Names and ancestry

  • Names can be rolled from the Primary, Secondary, Tertiary or Other community labels, or all of them, with an equal chance for each distinct ancestry. An explicit ancestry can name visitors, or be used before demographics are rolled.
  • Community ancestry labels roll from a Standard or Expanded pool you configure with the group and individual checkboxes. Apply is undoable; Cancel discards your edits. Other is a representative sample of up to three ancestries, and no-duplicate mode avoids names already used by other labels.
  • Labels that include Humans offer a culture choice: Random, one of eight Human cultures, or mixed Suel, Oeridian and Flan heritage. NPCs inherit the community choice unless you override it.
  • Rolled names stay editable, and their history, cultures and source labels are saved. In a Fortress, labels are GM context only; individual hobby slots can also have names.

Summaries, handouts and printing

Summary, in the settlement's identity panel, opens the viewer. Index card is a short card for map hovers. Cut sheet is one printable page. Full write-up has everything, including fortress plans and the side view. Handouts has shop and inn signs, plus menu cards built from fare and drinks saved in the DM toolkit (attach them to a place to give each inn its own menu). Atlas has a cover, every settlement's index card and, optionally, every cut sheet, printed as one booklet. Plain text gives copyable text.

DM / Player switches the audience. Player versions leave out hidden places, DM notes, objectives and rules text, and use each NPC's Public portrayal. Mark gaps shows red markers where something is still missing (DM version only). Inactive places and Record IDs are optional extras.

Print prints the current view, and each cut sheet fits one page on A4 or Letter. Copy text copies a plain version. Atlas in the top toolbar opens the viewer straight on the atlas.

Coat of arms

Every settlement gets arms chosen automatically from what it's known for, with the shield shape set by settlement type. In the identity panel, open Coat of arms to see a live preview and change the shield shape, division, colours, charge or charge colour. Anything left on Automatic follows the settlement. Lock keeps the current choices; Clear returns everything to automatic. Arms appear on the summaries and handouts and are visible to players.

Appendices and published NPCs

DM toolkit in the top toolbar opens an offline reference for Appendices A–D (pp. 438–455): location and fortress terms, location categories, encounters, rumors, tavern and hook builders, and useful tables. Roll previews or choose a printed outcome, then explicitly save to the current settlement. Use Attach to to assign fare, drinks or other toolkit results to a particular place; it defaults to the settlement. Tavern name previews and saved Tavern name results offer Use as this place’s name, with normal Undo. Codex location identities stay read-only. Previewing does not change records or Undo. Saved results have their own DM notes, roll trace and source pages; they remain DM-only in JSON and Markdown and are unaffected by Roll all.

Existing toolkit results without an attached place belong to the whole settlement; new results use the location selected in Attach to.

Encounter checks apply the current Crime modifier unless switched off. Villages and Fortresses have no prescribed urban-check table; explicitly select Trading Post/Town or City/Capital context to adapt one, or roll the encounter table directly. Rumors normally use the context’s eligible rows; disable that option for the full printed table. Follow-up rolls and rerolls remain visible in the trace.

Standard Fare on p. 448 prints d6 but lists eight rows. The builder uses d8 to include all eight outcomes, including follow-up rolls. The duplicate 100 result on p. 455 uses the selected 1%/0% magic policy. Alternate shop rolls are supplemental, not a change to settlement generation.

Published NPCs provides 120 profiles from Chapter Eight (pp. 182–227), searchable by profession and name. Browse or roll freely; Add editable DM draft creates a fresh NPC identity with source and game-statistic notes. Published drafts begin hidden from players. Add a safe public portrayal and choose visibility in NPCs & connections. They are separate from collection and Codex identities; adding one creates no automatic connection or campaign assertion.

Saving, undo and files

Open JSON replaces the collection and is undoable. Add from JSON keeps IDs and skips identical imports; conflicting IDs are rejected. Add as copies creates new draft identities and retains Codex references.

  • An edit is committed when you leave the field. Undo and Redo step through committed edits, bulk rolls, switching settlements, creating, duplicating, importing and removing.
  • The browser autosaves when it can, but autosave may not work for local files or private browsing. Save collection JSON regularly as your real backup.
  • Open JSON, Add from JSON, Add as copies and Export all DM Markdown are in the File menu.
  • Open JSON checks the whole file before replacing your collection, and can be undone. Add from JSON keeps IDs and skips identical imports; Add as copies makes new draft identities.
  • Save current workspace JSON exports only the current settlement and the identities it links.
  • DM Markdown starts with the overview, then grouped fields, places, people and regional ties, with record IDs in an appendix. It is a private reference for you.
  • Saved Player summary controls offer Automatic, Show or Hide on locations and NPCs. DM notes, objectives and old DM portrayal stay private; use Public portrayal for player-facing NPC text. Unresolved or inactive places and private rule fields are excluded even when Show is selected. Player descriptions omit dice ranges, modifiers and roll instructions; the DM data keeps the full rules text.
  • Add regional ties on Records and hooks in a location editor. Ties and hooks stay private unless explicitly shown. The Summary viewer uses these settings for its Player version.

Rule notes by settlement type

How this tool reads the book where the rules leave room for interpretation. Open the settlement type you're working on.

Trading Post
  • Roll the chapter's tables to create the Trading Post. Extra shops and services follow size-based counts; the General Store, the Inn and specialty bonuses are in addition to those.
  • Demographics: a roll of 10 overlaps two printed ranges; choose which applies.
  • A Shipwright needs significant water. If an automatic roll is rejected, it retries only when you press Roll.
  • Hospitality can't give the main inn Poor quality; a labeled local reroll policy handles this.
  • Magic shops already get a specialization from the d100; the d6 alternative is optional.
  • Intrigue is optional preparation. Optional appendix encounters and supporting tables are available in DM toolkit.
Village
  • Villages have no automatic Inn or General Store, and don't use the Trading Post quality, hired-help or magic-alternative tables.
  • Worship, gathering and other location counts follow the Village size formulas; both d2 results are stored for 2d2 counts.
  • Resource-related sites are optional GM selections, not a required inventory.
  • Age overlaps at 10; choose the printed range.
  • Hardship modifiers apply only to their listed attributes. Attribute-specific outcomes replace the shared outcome. Turning hardships off, or lowering likelihood, keeps the extra slots as inactive.
  • The example on p.29 wrongly labels outcome 6 Catastrophic; the table on p.30 correctly gives Heavy (−3).
  • Fervency is recorded once for the village; size and alignment are rolled per worship site.
  • Other-location result 100 keeps one burned or abandoned site with a former-type subroll. Local policy: automatic former-type rolls retry a 100 and keep every rejected attempt.
  • Harsh-weather suitability is your judgment; use explicit rerolls. “No Danger” hides the danger type without clearing it. Histories and rumors are draft preparation.
Town
  • Four default businesses sit outside the rolled commercial counts. All free bonus sites are additional.
  • Economic priority changes only the commercial size category; Merchant Monarch adds two commercial sites. The farm/resource roll count follows the town's actual size.
  • Port uses its own d6 environment. Production changes the specialty die to d4; earlier dice stay stored, and old d8 results that no longer fit are flagged.
  • Government leadership and the Farming specialty have explicit retry restrictions.
  • Hospitality uses its own d6 for the default inn, without wealth modifiers. Religious priority grants +5 only to its bonus worship site.
  • Changing a noncommercial or commercial category keeps separate subtype inputs for each.
  • Half-and-half needs an even commercial count; for an odd GM count, use random allocation or adjust it.
  • Optional Deserted and Isolated states trigger on totals of 0 or less before clamping. The book doesn't specify their effect on other tables, so resolve or switch off those modifiers yourself.
  • Market events don't add permanent businesses.
City
  • Districts roll condition, entry, crime, housing and notable counts. Slums uses an actual d4 for condition, read on the full d20 outcome bands.
  • Actual condition feeds crime; relative condition feeds location quality. Local encounter modifiers replace the citywide modifier.
  • All twelve district types have included and additional locations. Included locations sit outside the Size-based additional counts, and each duplicate has its own ID.
  • Temple classification and Temple hired help use their printed d6 splits. Merchant and Scholar fixed magic specializations use no die.
  • Quality is optional for all physical sites. Worship size, fervency and alignment are optional per site; turning them off keeps their inputs.
  • A location result of 1 or 20 rerolls the same slot and records a separate quality step. Repeated results accumulate within the current chain (a local interpretation).
  • Entertainment reserves one additional slot for your choice of venue.
  • Notability is capped by City Size and applies only to the first additional locations.
  • Production uses a d10 for the first outside slot only, retrying adjusted results of 1–4; the old d20 input and history stay saved.
  • Optional support-capacity scaling leaves the Size category and allocation counts unchanged.
  • Guild membership is a separate citywide d6 with saved member-count thresholds; a raw 1 is always No. Hired-help “Guild” describes provider size, not membership. Decisions stay fixed until you resolve them again.
  • City intrigue is optional preparation; its scene context and public awareness don't create campaign events or party knowledge.
Fortress

Foundations and materials

  • Roll the five foundation tables and the construction tables: Primary Building Materials, Unique Materials when needed, Resource Origin, Reason for Construction and Design Theme.
  • GM suitability controls material retries; if all six are excluded, the result is effectively Salvage, with the original dice kept.
  • For a fortress near an established settlement, choose its Environment yourself. Nested Environment keeps both the primary and inner context, with no extra roll. Active Volcano assumes suitable materials and resources, without a forced material or bonus.
  • Choosing a planned Keep, Castle or Stronghold rolls nothing and keeps the same physical Keep record. No price or headcount is inferred from Expense or Condition.

Entries and local impact

  • Alternate Entries (d20), Local Impact (d6) and optional Local Impact Change (d6) are available. Change is descriptive and doesn't update Local Impact; it starts off and keeps saved work when switched off.
  • Alternate-entry position is a provisional plan and creates no physical entry. Recent-age guidance is advisory.

Residents and garrison

  • Residents (d20), Relations (d12), Hobbies (d20) and Attitude (d6) are available; Age modifies Condition and Residents.
  • Optional Deserted applies at a Residents total of 0 or less before clamping. It makes occupancy and garrison details dormant without erasing saved work or NPCs. While Residents is unresolved, bulk occupancy rolls wait.
  • Hobbies can be one household roll, or named individual and group entries.
  • Garrison Size and Equipment use their printed d20 tables. Large and Maximum need Guard Bunks in the interior checklist. Any headcount is your own text; no items or combat statistics are created.

Issues, background and special features

  • Roll Current Issue and its Issue Severity. Ruin or Bare Bones adds a separate d6 structural issue, rolled before the normal issue. Peaceful skips only the normal issue's severity.
  • History (d10), Secrets (d12) and Oddities (d12) are draft prompts; they don't create entries, rooms, NPCs, items or effects. Back Door doesn't change Alternate Entries.
  • All eight Special Feature branches have their detail tables. Unknown Origin takes precedence over conflicting results: they keep their rolls but stop applying until you review them.

Keep and Castle

  • Keep structure: Shape d6, Base Size d20 and Keep BSM, exterior thickness d10, Floors d20, Raised Entrance d20 where eligible, and Entry Defenses d20. Interior dimensions exclude wall thickness; a cellar counts toward floors but not entrance eligibility.
  • Keep interior has a Furnishings d20 with Condition and Expense modifiers. The book's full room counts aren't generated; plan rooms yourself.
  • View map opens Keep floors or a Castle overview with a numbered structure register. Rolled measurements set the main dimensions; enclosure size, placement and roof shapes are illustrative. Drag structures on the five-foot grid; towers and gatehouses stay on their walls. Drag empty space to pan, or use arrow keys to move the selected structure. Locked items stay put. An invalid drop or Escape cancels a drag; a valid move is one Undo step. Layouts, locks and map labels save with the settlement. Use Reset map entry for placements flagged as no longer fitting. Export SVG saves the standard drawing with the selected grid, labels and legend.
  • Hand drawn redraws the map in ink, in the style of hand-drawn dungeon maps, on screen and in print; Export SVG keeps the standard drawing.
  • Side view shows a cross-section through the gate: walls and gatehouses as cut, towers and outbuildings beyond, the keep's floors and cellar, and the moat's depth. Heights come from the rolls; storey heights, roof pitch and motte height are illustrative and listed under the drawing. In a castle, heights are stretched so they read. Keep floors shows the keep at true scale, with rooms furnished for the functions you've confirmed on Keep interior. Download side view SVG saves the drawing.
  • For a planned Keep, the Castle tabs are hidden; tick Show inactive castle tabs to see them.
  • Castle foundations add Geographic Advantage d4, Style d20 and Castle Size/BSM d20. Choose a planned Castle or Stronghold to activate them; switching back to Keep keeps your work.
  • Castle review under Castle foundations checks General information, Keep structure and interior, and the Castle features. Castle tower-count and moat locks stay saved when switching to Keep. DM summaries include dimensions and wall references. The review doesn't check room layouts or Stronghold upgrades.
  • Castle walls, towers, curtain and magical defenses, the barbican, gatehouses and moat are available. Barracks and outbuildings use the Barracks & outbuildings tab: one barracks-location d20 and Castle BSM + 1 outbuilding-size d20 rolls. Extra Concentric walls do not multiply this allocation. Floor areas can be split between floors or pooled into freeform buildings; stacking does not create area. Confirm whether servants’ quarters are in the Keep; otherwise reserve a 3 × 5-square footprint in an outbuilding. Kitchens need the same minimum, and stables stay on the ground floor. These are area checks, not full room generation or geometry verification.

Versions and compatibility

Files saved by this version open in this version or later. Older saves upgrade automatically when opened, keeping IDs, notes, dice and connections.

Duplicate settlement

By default, draft NPCs become new people with copied notes. Codex references always keep their existing IDs. Sites and connections always receive new IDs. Dice, inactive work, ancestry preferences and notes are retained.

Opaque assertions, redirects and extensions stay verbatim. Copies include an ID mapping and a reminder to review embedded references to the original records.

Remove settlement

Remove and its owned sites/connections from this collection? Shared NPC records stay available. Undo restores the settlement.

Find and review

DM workspace directory and preparation checklist. Open an item to continue in the builder. Inactive book structures open their allocation section.

Rules and decisions cover active work. Writing prompts are optional preparation, not completion requirements.

DM preparation summary

Included ancestries

Standard uses the nine 2014 PHB races. Expanded is a curated 5e selection; setting-specific peoples and lineages have separate groups. Each checked entry gets an equal chance. Generic Elf and named elven variants are separate entries if both are included.

These are optional GM convenience rolls, outside Spectacular Settlements. Pool changes do not roll, clear, or replace labels. You can type other ancestries directly into the labels.
